title: Claude for health: what it can do, and how to reach a doctor from Claude
summary: Claude for health explained: what Claude's health connectors do, Anthropic's medical advice rules, and how to reach a FutureClinic doctor from Claude.
body_markdown:
Claude and ChatGPT Health provide instant explanations of test results and prepare questions for an appointment, while stopping short of diagnosing conditions or prescribing treatment. Adding FutureClinic to Claude lets you message an expert physician who can review your health context, diagnose your condition, and treat you if your doctor decides it's right for you, with no subscription required.


On FutureClinic, a specific doctor reads your whole case and answers you with a Human Signature: a short video or voice note recorded live for you. No form is approved in bulk. That same doctor can help with other problems in their specialty, and every FutureClinic doctor you see works from one medical record. We believe AI is a tool for doctors, and the doctor is in charge of every case. Most health problems have nuance and need one-to-one attention, and only an expert can tell when an AI has made a mistake or is heading to the wrong answer. FutureClinic's AI works behind the scenes like a chief resident, gathering your history so the doctor can move faster, and it never gives medical advice by itself. FutureClinic is not for emergencies; call 911, or call or text 988 in a mental-health crisis.


## What can Claude do with your health questions and records?


On January 11, 2026,[Anthropic introduced](https://www.anthropic.com/news/healthcare-life-sciences) personal health connections for US Claude Pro and Max subscribers (as of October 2026). Beta links with[Apple Health](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11869619-use-claude-with-ios-apps) and[Android Health Connect](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11869629-use-claude-with-android-apps) (updated August 25, 2026) give read-only access to activity, sleep, nutrition, and vitals. Directory connectors also link records and labs via[HealthEx](https://claude.com/marketplace/connectors/healthex) and[Function Health](https://claude.com/marketplace/connectors/function) (added January 2026),[Elfcare](https://claude.com/marketplace/connectors/elfcare) (added July 2026), and[athenahealth](https://claude.com/marketplace/connectors/athenahealth) in beta (added September 2026). Anthropic says Claude summarizes history, explains test results in plain language, spots patterns, prepares appointment questions, and does not train models on health data.


[Claude for Healthcare](https://claude.com/solutions/healthcare) (announced January 11, 2026; clarified February 7, 2026) is built for healthcare providers, payers, and health tech firms. Per Anthropic's[HIPAA guide](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13296973-hipaa-ready-enterprise-plans) (updated October 20, 2026), HIPAA-ready products and Business Associate Agreements apply only to Enterprise plans. Team and individual plans (Free, Pro, Max) cannot enable HIPAA; personal data is covered by Anthropic's[Consumer Health Data Privacy Policy](https://www.anthropic.com/legal/consumer-health-data-privacy-policy) (effective January 12, 2026).


## What does Anthropic say Claude should not do alone?


Anthropic's mobile help articles (updated August 25, 2026) state: "We are not a medical device and cannot provide medical guidance. Always consult a licensed professional." A[June 27, 2025 Anthropic study](https://www.anthropic.com/research/how-people-use-claude-for-support-advice-and-companionship) noted that Claude cannot provide medical diagnoses, and the athenahealth listing notes it "doesn't diagnose conditions or make clinical decisions."


Anthropic's[Usage Policy](https://www.anthropic.com/legal/aup) requires human oversight. Under the September 15, 2025 policy, medical diagnosis and patient care require that "a qualified professional in that field must review the content or decision." Under the update taking effect November 12, 2026 (see the[October 8, 2026 post](https://www.anthropic.com/news/2026-usage-policy-update) ), diagnosing conditions, adjusting medications or doses, or interpreting symptoms or labs for a treatment plan requires that "A qualified person must meaningfully review a High-risk AI Recommendation," with power to change it and disclosure that AI was used. The[Software Directory Policy](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13145358-anthropic-software-directory-policy) (updated October 27, 2026) applies these rules to all healthcare connectors.
